```yaml
name: PR Delta Validation

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  validate-delta:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Ensure origin/main is up to date
        run: git fetch origin main

      - name: Install Salesforce CLI
        run: npm install -g @salesforce/cli

      - name: Install sfdx-git-delta plugin
        run: sf plugins install sfdx-git-delta --force

      - name: Generate delta manifest
        run: |
          mkdir -p changed-sources
          sf sgd source delta --from origin/main --to HEAD --output-dir changed-sources

      - name: Authenticate to production
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.SF_JWT_KEY }}" > server.key
          sf org login jwt --instance-url https://login.salesforce.com \
            --client-id "${{ secrets.SF_CONSUMER_KEY }}" \
            --username "${{ secrets.SF_USERNAME }}" \
            --jwt-key-file server.key --alias prod
          rm server.key

      - name: Validate deployment with destructive changes
        run: |
          sf project deploy validate \
            --target-org prod \
            --manifest changed-sources/package/package.xml \
            --post-destructive-changes changed-sources/destructiveChanges/destructiveChanges.xml \
            --test-level RunLocalTests \
            --wait 120
```

Key points:

- `--post-destructive-changes` requires `--manifest`, so the deploy uses the manifest sfdx-git-delta generated (`changed-sources/package/package.xml`) without `--source-dir` — exactly one source specifier. The manifest lists only the added/changed components, and those files exist in the checked-out workspace, so the CLI resolves them from the project root.
- `--output-dir` (not the deprecated `--output`) is used for the delta output directory.
- `--post-destructive-changes` passes the `destructiveChanges.xml` for deleted components, so deletions are processed after the other components deploy.
- `--wait 120` waits up to 120 minutes; a failed validation exits non-zero and fails the workflow.

Key correction — muting permission set semantics: in a muting permission set, a permission flagged **`true`** is the one being **muted** (removed), and permissions flagged `false` are left untouched. My previous files used inverted values, which is why nothing was actually muted (contractors could still delete) and why the dependency validation failed once the set was attached to the group ("To mute Read, first mute Create, Edit, Delete, View All Records, and Modify All Records" — that error was triggered by my inconsistent flag combination).

Now, respecting Salesforce's muting dependency rules:

- **Delete only**: `allowDelete=true` mutes just the Delete object permission. Delete has no permissions depending on it, so it can be muted standalone. Create, Edit, Read, View All Records and Modify All Records stay `false` (unmuted), so contractors keep create/edit/read/View All access.
